title: Add code-health check, status table, and design-review cadence
summary: Retry of 20261026-042558-5p65: add code_health.rs measuring per-file production lines, longest function, 7-day churn, failure citations and test run time. Show it in athena status with thresholds, queue one structural-pass request per breaching file, run it after landings, and queue a self-contained design-review request every 10 landings. Audience is Sri and the verifier.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for each behavior; cargo test and clippy clean.
Decide on syn versus hand scan for function length and record it.
Criteria run cargo test on behaviors, not existence.
Breaches are caught and queued without being pointed out.
Status table verified by rendering it in a test.
Docs and decisions written for outside readers.
Dependency on the nonexistent design-review role is removed by defining its content here.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: No design-review role or text for request 20261017-205558-dn2e exists in the repo; this job defines the review content itself and does not depend on it.
Dedup and cadence are derived from records and the request queue, not a counter, so running both hooks for one job does not double count.
If no earlier design-review request exists, the cadence baseline is the current landing so the first review does not fire immediately on existing history.
Function length is measured with an adopted parser crate (syn) or a simple scan; the choice is recorded in docs/decisions.md.
No athena.toml field is added; thresholds are constants in code_health.rs.
Hooks run from steward note_finished (run.rs) and Athena::land_pr in gh.rs.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test: a code_health test with fixture source files and landing records asserts per-file production line count (excluding #[cfg(test)] modules), longest function length, landings in the last 7 days, and failure/rejection citations.

Run cargo test: tests show a breach of each threshold (file over 2000 lines, function over 200 lines, over 1500 lines with 5 or more landings in a week) is reported and a file under the thresholds is not flagged.

Run cargo test: on a breach exactly one structural-pass request is queued for that file, citing the measured numbers; running again, or with an open structural-pass request for that file, queues none.

Run cargo test: the design-review request is queued at high priority at the 10th landing since the last review and not at the 9th; its text states what to review (module size, churn, duplicated logic, boundaries), the output (findings page and follow-up requests with acceptance bullets) and when it is done.
Run cargo test: with no earlier review request the first design review does not fire at once on existing history.
Run cargo test: a test of the Athena::land_pr path shows the code-health check is invoked, and fails if the hook is removed; the finished-job hook is likewise shown.

Run cargo test: the rendered athena status output contains the code-health table with each file's lines, longest function, weekly landings, citations, thresholds, whether over, and test suite run time.
cargo clippy with -D warnings and cargo fmt --check are clean and cargo test passes.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry, and docs/decisions.md records the thresholds, the buy-versus-build call on measuring function length, and the 10-landing cadence.

out_of_scope: Creating a design-review role or prompt beyond the queued request's text
Actually performing structural refactors of breaching files
departures: Larger scope than typical (new module, two hooks, status rendering, request text) raises cost and time; the earlier failure was a planning misread now addressed.
urgent_reason: Cuts a repeat of the failed attempt (a planning stop over a missing design-review role) and the redo work it caused.
